sections.html:
Kaysville sits in Davis County, inside the Ogden-Clearfield metro, bordered by Layton on the north, Fruit Heights on the east and Farmington on the south. At the 2020 census it had 32,945 residents, 8,958 households and 9,175 housing units, with only 2.4% of the units vacant. An empty or neglected house therefore draws notice on a street full of year-round neighbors.

This is a family city. Median age is 29.9, and about 52.4% of households are raising children under 18. After an owner moves away or dies, the house can sit out of step with its block while taxes, insurance and utilities keep coming due.

sections.h2: Jobs, commuting and moving on a deadline
sections.html:
Many Davis County residents commute into Salt Lake County, and Hill Air Force Base, at the county's northern end, employs more people than anyone else. The Davis School District, Lagoon Amusement Park and Lifetime Products follow. A job change often brings a move with a hard deadline, so certainty about timing matters.

  • Relocating for work? Get any buyer's closing date confirmed in writing.
  • If the house must be empty before you leave, it can be sold as it stands with no staging.
  • Heirs living out of state can complete a sale through a title company and never visit Kaysville.

Public schools come from the Davis School District, and Davis High School is the local high school. The city supplies garbage pickup, curbside recycling, green waste recycling, power, pressure irrigation, storm water and water. Sewer comes from Central Davis Sewer instead of the city. Kaysville City Power is at 721 W Old Mill Lane, phone 801-544-8925, the number to call when you transfer power during a sale.

Kaysville bases permit fees on project value, adds a 1% state education fee and a 25% plan check fee, and posts a fee schedule online. Impact fees apply to new single-family homes, and a few typical amounts are below.

Permit or feeKaysville amount
Parks and recreation impact fee, new home$4,480
Central Davis Sewer fee, new home$2,400
North Davis Sewer fee, new home$3,454.03
Basement finish or remodel permit$245.70
Furnace, A/C or water heater permit$65.65

Work that has not begun in 180 days, or that stalls for 180 days, voids the permit and costs you the construction bond. Sellers with a half-finished basement and a dead permit may hear from a mortgage-backed buyer that it must be closed out first. A cash buyer can accept the house as is and settle the permit later.

sections.h2: Can I rent out part of my Kaysville house?
sections.html:
Internal accessory dwelling units are allowed in Kaysville when the owner makes the main home or the unit a primary residence. City Code 17-31-3 sets out the rules.

  • Expect a permit requirement if the occupant is not a relative.
  • Plan on a separate paved parking space beyond the two-car garage and two-car driveway.
  • Detached structures, such as an apartment over a garage or a granny flat, cannot be used as a dwelling.
  • Additions or remodels done to create the unit need a building permit.

Bought a house with a basement apartment? Check that it was set up under these rules. A house leased out entirely, apartment included, may not qualify, because an owner must live there.

Valuation notices leave the Davis County offices at the end of July. Under state law the appeal deadline is the later of September 15 or 45 days after the auditor provides notice, and Tax Administration can confirm the exact date before you file.

The tax rate cannot be appealed; market value can. Appeals go to the Board of Equalization, which is the Davis County Commission acting on recommendations from hearing officers it appoints. Bring closing documents, a certified appraisal or comparable sales. An agent who files for an owner needs a notarized authorization.

  • Tax Administration is at 61 South Main Street, Room 101, Farmington.
  • Phone: 801-451-3331 or 801-451-3329.
  • A late appeal may still be heard by the board when there are extenuating circumstances.

A qualifying home is taxed on 55% of market value under Utah's primary residential exemption. Because the buyer has to submit a new application after the sale, mention that step early.

sections.h2: How a cash sale of a Kaysville house works
sections.html:
Cash sales close at a title company, which has the deed recorded by the Davis County Recorder. No loan means a shorter list: a purchase contract, a title search, signatures on a settlement statement, then recording.

A deed in Utah must name the grantees, carry a mailing address for assessment and taxation, and include a legal description that meets state standards. The recorder may also ask for the parcel's tax identification number.

If the sale lands partway through the year, the title company usually divides that year's tax between you and the buyer, and you can ask to see the split before closing day.

sections.h2: Getting ready for the title company
sections.html: A title company is the neutral party in a Kaysville sale. It collects the signed contract, searches the record for liens, back taxes and ownership gaps, and prepares the settlement statement that shows who is paid what. Show up with a government ID and the names of everyone on the deed. If a spouse, an heir or a trustee has to sign, tell the title officer ahead of time so each person can be scheduled, and ask whether notary pages can be sent by mail for anyone who lives far away. Review the settlement statement a day early so any question about the tax split, a payoff or a permit lien is answered before you sit down to sign.

sections.h2: Situations that call for a quick sale
sections.html:
• Inherited houses that need updating before a normal listing.
  • Basement apartments added without a permit or the required parking space.
  • Lapsed building permits with a forfeited bond.
  • Owners who must relocate and cannot manage showings from afar.

On any route, weigh your net after repairs, commission and carrying costs, and read each contract before signing.

If you decide on a direct sale, the process runs in a few simple steps. You send the address and describe the house, including any permit or parking issues. We review it against nearby sales and make an offer. If you accept, a title company runs the title search, confirms what is owed and sets signing. You sign, the deed is recorded, and the proceeds are paid out after any payoff or tax balance. There are no showings, no staging and no lender to wait on.

Gather the deed, the latest tax notice, permit records for any remodel and a mortgage payoff statement first. Those papers answer most of what a buyer and title officer will ask.

faqs.q: What is the property tax appeal deadline in Davis County?
faqs.a: The later of September 15 or 45 days after the valuation notice. Tax Administration, at 801-451-3331, can confirm the date before you file.

faqs.q: Can I put an apartment in my Kaysville basement?
faqs.a: Yes, as an internal accessory dwelling unit, provided you live in the main home or the unit. Add a separate paved parking space, and get a permit if the tenant is not a relative.

faqs.q: Who provides sewer service in Kaysville?
faqs.a: Central Davis Sewer provides sewer service, not the city. The city provides water, power, pressure irrigation, garbage, recycling and storm water.

faqs.q: Do building permits expire in Kaysville?
faqs.a: Yes. Work that fails to start within 180 days, or stops for 180 days, ends the permit. The bond is forfeited and a new application follows.

faqs.q: How many people live in Kaysville?
faqs.a: The 2020 count was 32,945, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 33,307.
